transcript.content: I'm having trouble sleeping at night—waking up around 2 or 3 in the morning and can't get back to sleep. It's been happening pretty regularly for the past couple of weeks, and I'm wondering if it might be related to my naltrexone or one of my other medications. I'd like to know what might be causing it and if there's anything I can adjust.

Hi Maggie, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality.

Sleep disruption can definitely be a side effect of some medications, and it's smart to look into this. However, I can't advise on whether to adjust or stop any of your medications — that needs your doctor's review, especially since naltrexone and sertraline (which you take for recovery support) can both affect sleep in different ways.

Let me get you connected with Dr. Rodriguez so he can assess what's going on. Would you prefer a quick virtual call today, or would you rather send him a message that he can review and get back to you on?

I'd really prefer an in-person visit if that's possible. I find that face-to-face conversations with my doctors are more helpful, especially when we're discussing my medications and how they're affecting me. Can you check what Dr. Rodriguez has available in the next week or so?
I'll check what's available for you with Dr. Rodriguez over the next few days.
